note: The charter and the class assignment the featureset census reads. Declared, not inferred: bin/feature-census.mjs refuses to guess, so a (surface, key) pair absent from `groups` below is reported `unclassified` rather than quietly filed as core. Change this file to change a verdict, and the census output records which charter version it read.
charter: commitwork runs a repository's GitHub Actions CI locally, then scans that repository for security defects with a portable baseline of third-party and own-built checks.
It runs that baseline on a schedule over a fleet of repositories, keeps the per-finding history, and reports what each check actually measured — including what it could not measure.
It turns those findings into remediation work: a per-area queue, an issue tracker, suggested fixes a person approves, and an adjudication record of what was judged and why.
It packages the same evidence for compliance audiences (EU CRA, SOC 2, NIST 800-53) and exposes it to coding agents over MCP.
Its promise is reporting that survives scrutiny: a result it did not measure is never published as a pass, and never as a finding.

membershipTests.core: Delete this group and a sentence of the charter above becomes false. Mechanically: the group is named in `charter`, and some other core group reads its output.
membershipTests.extension: Builds on a core group through a public seam (a route, a store, a manifest), is complete on the inventory's own fields (entry point + tests + docs), and could be removed without editing any core group.
membershipTests.ring-outward: Serves an adjacent audience or an adjacent job. No core group reads its output, so removing it changes who commitwork is for, not whether it works.
membershipTests.fragment: Reachable, but the inventory shows a completeness field missing: no test names it, no doc names it, or (a panel view) it has no durable URL. A decision, never a deletion.
membershipTests.orphan: Defined in the tree and wired into nothing that runs: an unmounted route table, a view no chrome links to, a descriptor with no handler, a module nothing names, an override nothing reads outside tests.

priorityNote: orphan and fragment are MECHANICAL and outrank the declared class, because a group can be core in intent and still have an entry point nothing reaches. The declared class is what the group WOULD be once complete, and the census records both so the disposition is legible.
populationNote: config-flag is inventoried but NOT censused: an environment override is a parameter OF a feature, not a feature. Classing 626 of them would put 90% of the census rows on things no reader calls a feature, and the per-flag documentation gap is reported as its own count instead.
experimentalNote: Every ring-outward group carries "experimental": true and a "flag" id from experimentalFlags. A flag is ON unless switched off: the panel Settings view (Experimental features, POST /api/features), the experimentalFeatures setting, CW_FEATURE_<ID>=on|off for one flag (dashes become underscores, uppercased), or CW_EXPERIMENTAL=on|off for all. Per-flag env beats CW_EXPERIMENTAL, which beats the store. An off flag is refused by the route dispatcher (404), hidden from panel navigation, listed under 'experimental (off)' in CLI help and refused when run, omitted from the MCP tool list and refused when called, and not installed by monitor/install-agents.mjs. cli-script groups have no runtime gate: the flag is recorded and the census reports it unenforced. A flag may also be declared with no group and optional "views" (panel view ids): it is gated in code through featureEnabled()/gateFeature() and needs no other declaration. lib/feature-charter.mjs reads this declaration; lib/feature-flags.mjs resolves it.
